# Compare transcript structures, then add evidence

This example compares human full-length AS3MT, a **paper-defined d2d3
reconstruction**, and chimpanzee full-length AS3MT. The reconstructed human
transcript skips exons 2 and 3. We first compare the transcript models, then
inspect DNA at the exon-1 repeat.

Human coordinates use **GRCh38**; chimpanzee coordinates use **Pan_tro_3.0**.
Each assembly has its own genomic axis. All inputs are bundled and work offline.

# Prepare one comparative Syn object

The loader returns a `SynSpecies`. It contains two `SynIndividual` objects,
their feature annotations and a named human-chimpanzee alignment. Original
repeat sequences, source specifications and supporting evidence stay in the
object's metadata.

```{r as3mt-load, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(ggexon)
library(ggplot2)

demo_dir <- system.file("extdata", "as3mt", package = "ggexon")
source(file.path(demo_dir, "load-as3mt-example.R"), local = TRUE)
source(file.path(demo_dir, "as3mt-object-data.R"), local = TRUE)
as3mt <- load_as3mt_example(demo_dir)

class(as3mt)
individual_names(as3mt)
nrow(pairwise_alignment_data(as3mt, alignment = "human_chimp"))
```

The alignment contains **37 ungapped LASTZ blocks**, selected from the two
highest original identity categories.

## Prepare reusable annotation views

Prepare exon labels and store two views of the aligned VNTR DNA on the same
object. The combined view keeps the full alignment and selects the terminal
repeat for the callouts. The close-up view selects just the terminal repeat.
Query the combined view to count the chimpanzee gap columns across the full
alignment.

```{r as3mt-prepare}
as3mt <- prepare_as3mt_example(as3mt)

vntr <- as3mt_evidence(as3mt)$vntr
donor_boundaries <- data.frame(
  sequence = names(vntr$donor_after), position = unname(vntr$donor_after),
  label = "E1 donor | intron 1"
)
as3mt <- prepare_alignseq(
  as3mt, vntr$aligned, vntr$anchors, reference = vntr$reference,
  name = "as3mt_vntr", regions = vntr$regions, details = vntr$details,
  flank = vntr$flank, boundaries = donor_boundaries
)
as3mt <- prepare_alignseq(
  as3mt, vntr$aligned, vntr$anchors, reference = vntr$reference,
  name = "as3mt_vntr_detail", regions = vntr$details, boundaries = donor_boundaries
)

head(as3mt_plot_data(as3mt, "exon_labels")[,
  c("id", "exon", "start", "end", "label")])
chimp_dna <- query_alignseq(as3mt, name = "as3mt_vntr", individual = "chimp")
sum(chimp_dna$base == "-")
dna_detail <- query_alignseq(as3mt, name = "as3mt_vntr_detail")
dna_detail[dna_detail$boundary_after, c("individual", "chr", "position", "boundary_label")]
```

`prepare_as3mt_example()` is an example helper. It derives exon labels from
stored CDS and UTR features and retains full-reference exon numbers.
`as3mt_plot_data()` retrieves those labels. `prepare_alignseq()` stores
aligned bases, difference events and donor boundaries under each view name.
`query_alignseq()` inspects the stored rows in their native genomic
coordinates. The transcript, alignment and DNA layers resolve their data
from the Syn object. Refresh the exon labels after editing the feature
models. Prepare the DNA views again after changing their aligned strings,
anchors or selected windows.

# Compare the transcript models

Human d2d3 is orange and sits above full-length AS3MT in blue. Chimpanzee AS3MT is grey.
Gold identifies E2/E3 in the full-length human model. The reconstructed
transcript omits these two exons and retains **E1 and
E4–E11**, including its untranslated first exon.

Define the colours and text settings used below:

```{r as3mt-style}
base_size <- 8
base_family <- "serif"
text_mm <- base_size / ggplot2::.pt
identity_bands <- levels(as3mt_evidence(as3mt)$links$identity_band)
fill_colours <- c(
  human_full = "#0072B2", human_short = "#D55E00", chimp = "#64748B",
  skipped_exons = "#E69F00",
  stats::setNames(scales::pal_viridis()(length(identity_bands)), identity_bands)
)
```

Build the plot directly from the object. `compress_introns = FALSE` disables
`geom_exon2()`'s own schematic spacing. The shared x scale then compresses
introns **30-fold**, preserving exon widths and keeping links and labels
aligned with the transcript models. Select the `human` and `chimp`
annotation panels explicitly.

```{r as3mt-pairwise, fig.alt="The reconstructed human d2d3 row sits above the full-length human model. The full-length model includes gold E2 and E3. Genomic ribbons connect the human and chimpanzee panels on compressed axes.", fig.cap="Transcript models and ungapped DNA similarity. Introns are compressed 30-fold."}
transcript_plot <- ggexon(as3mt) +
  geom_exon2(
    aes(xmin = xmin - 0.5, xmax = xmax + 0.5, ymin = isoform_y,
        transcripts = transcript_name, fill = exon_class),
    species = c("human", "chimp"),
    annotation_type = "all", exon_height = 0.42, compress_introns = FALSE,
    utr_height = 0.35, cds_height = 1, intron_shape = "chevron",
    arrow_width = 1e-8, colour = NA, transcript_backbone_colour = "grey40"
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = function(model) as3mt_plot_data(model, "exon_labels"),
    aes(x = x, y = y, label = label),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, size = text_mm, family = base_family
  ) +
  geom_nuclink(
    aes(fill = identity_band), alignment = "human_chimp",
    colour = NA, alpha = 0.25, inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  facet_genomics(
    vars(track), scales = "free_x", ncol = 1, link_panel_height = 0.35,
    link_axis = "none", link_strip = "blank", annotation_axis = "all",
    strip.position = "left",
    labeller = as_labeller(c(human = "Human\nGRCh38",
      chimp = "Chimpanzee\nPan_tro_3.0", link_human_chimp = ""))
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = fill_colours, breaks = tail(identity_bands, 2),
    name = "LASTZ identity (%)"
  ) +
  scale_x_ggexon_genomic(
    intron_factor = 30, guide = guide_x_ggexon_piecewise(by = "panel")
  ) +
  scale_panel_annotation("free_y", limits = list(human = c(0.15, 3.1), chimp = c(0.15, 1.8))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL,
    caption = "Thick boxes show CDS and thin boxes show UTR. The upper human row is the d2d3 reconstruction.") +
  theme_ggexon_track(
    base_size = base_size, base_family = base_family,
    show_x_axis = TRUE, show_x_grid = FALSE, show_legend = TRUE
  ) +
  theme_ggexon_side_strips("left", base_size = base_size, face = "plain") +
  theme(
    strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0),
    legend.position = "bottom", panel.spacing.y = grid::unit(0.35, "lines"),
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0)
  )
transcript_plot
```

The two ribbon colours represent **97.1–98.3%** and **98.3–100%** LASTZ
identity. The 37 blocks split into 57 polygon pieces at scale boundaries.
These links show genomic DNA similarity.

# Inspect DNA at the exon-1 repeat

The selected human reference contains three **36-bp VNTR** units; the chimp
reference has one imperfect homolog, with 34 of 36 matching bases. The terminal
unit spans 24 exonic and 12 intronic bases. Both references retain the **GT** donor:

```text
CCTGAGTCGCAGGCCGAGGAGACA | GTGAGTGCGCGC
         human exon 1  | intron 1
```

The aligned strings and genomic anchors are stored in `as3mt`. The preparation
uses the specified human reference. A `-` is an alignment gap and consumes
no genomic base. The donor-anchored alignment,
verified against the bundled FASTAs, places 72 chimp gap columns opposite
two human repeat copies.

For a close-up, use two annotation panels and change the windows on a copy
of the same Syn object. `geom_alignseq()` reads the named
`as3mt_vntr_detail` view and connects each sequence to its selected transcript.

```{r as3mt-alignseq-rows, fig.height=5, fig.alt="Terminal repeat DNA above human and chimpanzee exon-1 models. Aligned bases are grey and mismatches orange. A donor mark divides 24 exonic and 12 intronic bases."}
sequence_model <- as3mt
species_layout(sequence_model) <- SynLayout(
  panels = data.frame(PANEL = 1:2, ROW = 1:2, COL = 1,
    track = c("human", "chimp"), species = c("human", "chimp"),
    panel_type = "annotation", SCALE_X = 1:2, SCALE_Y = 1:2),
  free = list(x = TRUE, y = TRUE)
)
sequence_model <- set_panel_xlim(
  sequence_model, individual = c("human", "chimp"),
  xlim = list(human = c(102869568, 102869608), chimp = c(104324209, 104324249)),
  xlim_chr = c(human = "chr10", chimp = "chr10")
)
sequence_plot <- ggexon(sequence_model) +
  geom_exon2(
    aes(xmin = xmin - 0.5, xmax = xmax + 0.5, ymin = isoform_y,
        transcripts = transcript_name, fill = exon_class),
    annotation_type = "all", exon_height = 0.42,
    compress_introns = FALSE, utr_height = 0.35, cds_height = 1,
    arrow_width = 1e-8, colour = NA
  ) +
  geom_alignseq(
    alignment = "as3mt_vntr_detail", mode = "rows",
    anchor = "transcript", transcripts = c(human = "human_short", chimp = "chimp"),
    colour_scheme = "difference", size = text_mm, family = "mono"
  ) +
  facet_genomics(vars(track), scales = "free_x", ncol = 1,
    strip.position = "left", labeller = as_labeller(c(human = "Human", chimp = "Chimpanzee"))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = fill_colours, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_number(big.mark = ","),
    n.breaks = 3, oob = scales::oob_keep) +
  scale_panel_annotation("free_y", limits = list(human = c(0.3, 4.4), chimp = c(0.3, 3.2))) +
  labs(x = "Assembly-specific chr10 genomic coordinates", y = NULL,
    caption = "Terminal VNTR unit: E1 (24 nt) | intron 1 (12 nt).") +
  theme_ggexon_track(base_size = base_size, base_family = base_family,
    show_x_axis = TRUE, show_x_grid = FALSE) +
  theme(strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0),
    plot.margin = margin(6, 40, 6, 6))
sequence_plot
```

Sequence letters are equally spaced schematically. Their connector anchors
use genomic positions. Grey marks aligned bases, orange marks mismatches,
and red marks indels. The DNA colours are independent of transcript colours.

# Combine the evidence

Add the terminal-repeat callouts to `transcript_plot` using the
`as3mt_vntr` preparation. Each connector follows the transcript geometry on
its compressed genomic axis. The human callout attaches to d2d3 and the
chimpanzee callout attaches to its single model. `show_markers = FALSE`
hides event glyphs and their labels while preserving the sequence colours.

Set panel heights in the order of human annotation, genomic links and
chimpanzee annotation. The chimpanzee panel is half the height of the human
panel, and the link panel stays compact.

```{r as3mt-alignseq, warning=FALSE, fig.height=6, fig.alt="Human d2d3 sits above the full-length human model. Genomic ribbons connect the human and chimpanzee panels. DNA callouts attach to d2d3 and the chimpanzee transcript.", fig.cap="One comparative Syn object supplies transcript structures, genomic links and DNA detail."}
combined_plot <- transcript_plot +
  geom_alignseq(
    alignment = "as3mt_vntr", anchor = "transcript",
    transcripts = c(human = "human_short", chimp = "chimp"),
    show_markers = FALSE, colour_scheme = "difference", size = text_mm, family = "mono"
  ) +
  scale_panel_annotation("free_y", limits = list(human = c(0.15, 4.1), chimp = c(0.2, 2.8))) +
  theme(panel.heights = grid::unit(c(1, 0.35, 0.5), "null")) +
  labs(caption = "The chimp sequence is 72 bp shorter than the selected human VNTR reference. d2d3 is reconstructed.")
combined_plot
```

Cai et al. tested otherwise matched **two- and three-repeat human minigenes**;
three repeats produced more d2d3. This supports repeat-dependent splicing
regulation, but does not establish sufficiency for the isoform's evolutionary
origin. The human allele experiment differs by **36 bp**. The **−72 bp**
difference compares the selected chimp and human references. The two base
differences in the chimp homolog provide sequence context.

# Sources and reproducibility

- [Li et al. (2016), doi:10.1038/nm.4096](https://doi.org/10.1038/nm.4096):
  d2d3 reconstruction and repeat sequence.
- [Cai et al. (2021), doi:10.1093/schbul/sbaa098](https://doi.org/10.1093/schbul/sbaa098):
  human VNTR minigene comparison.

The installed `extdata/as3mt` directory contains all inputs, example preparation
functions and provenance. `as3mt_evidence(as3mt)` retains the original repeat
sequences, source specifications and alignment evidence for inspection.

Repository preparation and export scripts are in `data-raw/as3mt`. Genomic
ribbons use LASTZ `--nogapped --chain` blocks. Existing figure-export helpers
remain available;
the plotting commands used in this tutorial are shown above.
